messages:
erin: Heads up — seeing a bunch of gang-scheduling failures in ap-southeast1 rack-B, root cause looks like NVLink throughput drop on 3 nodes. Pods get Pending and then OOM/killed during attach.
sam: Ugh. Any recent kernel or firmware pushes to that rack?
erin: Not since yesterday. I can repro locally: `kubectl describe pod` shows attach timeout then eviction. Sample: 
```
Warning  FailedAttachVolume  30s   attach-detach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "gpu-kv-cache" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
```
leo: Did we taint those nodes? I remember we applied `nvlink-degraded:NoSchedule` last week to one zone for testing.
erin: Only 1 node had the taint, but these failures are across 3 nodes in same rack and they don't have the taint.
ops-jen: Oncall alert fired at 12:03. oncall-bot posted a perf spike: 
oncall-bot: ALERT[3260009800] nvlink_throughput_drop rack-b: 60% drop in link throughput vs baseline for 5m, affected nodes: node-b-17,node-b-18,node-b-22
sam: Can you grab `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `dmesg | tail -n 50` from node-b-17? Also check NIC/PCIe errors.
erin: Pasted quick outputs: 
```
# nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU0    GPU1    CPU Affinity    NVLINK
GPU0     X      0-23            10GB/s
GPU1    10GB/s   X              10GB/s
```
`dmesg` shows repeated `pcie link retrain` and a couple `AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error` lines.
leo: That smells like intermittent PCIe or switch flakiness — could be firmware/regression on the NVSwitch. Any rack-level maintenance?
ops-jen: Nothing scheduled. I'm thinking we should cordon the 3 nodes, migrate canaries, then repro with stress tests. Cordon command: 
```
kubectl cordon node-b-17 && kubectl drain node-b-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
erin: Will do. Also, cost angle — these failed attach retries are driving up Dedicated job runtime/costs. We had 12% extra GPU-hours on that region last 6h. Not huge yet but trending.
sam: If it's NVSwitch firmware, vendor has a beta rolled out last month. Check image tags in node firmware inventory.
leo: I can pull BMC logs and cross-check firmware versions. If firmware mismatch, escalate to HW-eng/vendor.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Incident created #INC-3260 with priority P2.
ops-jen: Plan: cordon+drain affected nodes, failover running jobs to other racks, collect BMC/dmesg/nvtop logs, open vendor ticket with logs and AER entries. I'll own the failover.
erin: Cordoned node-b-17, drain in progress. Will capture logs to /tmp/nvlink-dump-node-b-17.tar.gz and upload to the incident.
sam: After failover, we should run a controlled burn-in for 30m on a spare node to ensure link stability before rejoining.
leo: Agreed. If vendor ack is slow, we might need to decommission these nodes from Dedicated pool temporarily and move commitments — ops, can we reassign capacity?
ops-jen: Yes, we have 2 cold racks we can warm and shift capacity to. Will coordinate with sales for capacity commitment adjustments.
erin: Updating incident with initial logs. Will ping once drain is complete. :white_check_mark:
